title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
summary: We study empirical scaling laws for language model performance on the cross-entropy loss. The loss scales as a power-law with model size, dataset size, and the amount of compute used for training, with some trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
summary: We present Constitutional AI, a method for training AI systems to be helpful, harmless, and honest using a set of principles and AI-generated feedback rather than human feedback alone. We demonstrate the approach produces models that are less harmful while remaining helpful.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
summary: We report the development of GPT-4, a large multimodal model capable of processing image and text inputs and producing text outputs. GPT-4 demonstrates human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
summary: We introduce Codex, a GPT language model fine-tuned on publicly available code from GitHub, and study its Python code-writing capabilities. A distinct version of Codex solves 28.8% of the HumanEval benchmark problems. We release the HumanEval dataset to evaluate the correctness of model-generated code.

title: Uber deploys LLM-based code review at scale, reduces review time by 35%
summary: Uber engineering blog post detailing their 18-month rollout of LLM-assisted code review across 4,000 engineers. Includes methodology, A/B test results showing 35% reduction in review cycle time, false positive rates, and lessons learned from three failed approaches before finding what worked.

title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
summary: We introduce the MMLU benchmark covering 57 subjects including mathematics, history, law, and medicine. We find that while most recent models show near random-chance accuracy, the largest GPT-3 model improves over random chance by almost 20 percentage points on average.

title: Chip Huyen: Lessons from six months running LLMs in production
summary: After deploying LLM-powered features to 2M users, here is what actually broke: latency variance was 10x worse than benchmarks suggested, context window management consumed more engineering time than model selection, and our eval suite caught only 40% of production failures. Detailed post-mortem with specific numbers.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
summary: We analyze how language model performance degrades as a function of where relevant information appears in the input context. Models perform significantly worse when relevant information is in the middle of the context versus the beginning or end, with performance dropping up to 20 percentage points.

title: Simon Willison: What I learned building 50 LLM applications
summary: Detailed technical retrospective on building 50 real LLM-powered applications over two years. Covers prompt engineering patterns that work, common failure modes, cost management, and why most demos fail in production. Includes specific code examples and measured outcomes.
